::: {.pi-hero}
## 🛤️ Path Integrals in Quantum Mechanics & QFT

A complete, pedagogically rigorous journey through Feynman's path integral formulation — from the simple question *"how does a particle get from A to B?"* all the way to Euclidean field theory, instantons, and the bridge to statistical mechanics. Every derivation is shown, every concept is motivated, every "why" is answered.

::: {.hero-badges}
<span class="hero-badge">📖 Feynman & Hibbs</span>
<span class="hero-badge">📖 Shankar</span>
<span class="hero-badge">📖 Zinn-Justin</span>
<span class="hero-badge">📖 Kleinert</span>
<span class="hero-badge">🔬 15 Modules</span>
<span class="hero-badge">🎯 Wick Rotation</span>
<span class="hero-badge">🌀 Instantons</span>

<!-- COURSE OVERVIEW -->

::: {.roadmap-box}
#### 🗺️ What You Will Learn

This course takes you on a complete journey through the **path integral formulation of quantum mechanics**:

1. **Foundation** (Modules 1–3): What propagators are, Feynman's "sum over all paths" idea, and your first complete path integral — the free particle
2. **The Machine** (Modules 4–7): Rigorous derivation of the path integral from operators, the harmonic oscillator, functional calculus, and Gaussian integrals — the mathematical toolkit
3. **Classical Meets Quantum** (Module 8): How classical mechanics *emerges* from the path integral via stationary phase
4. **Into Euclidean Territory** (Modules 9–11): Wick rotation, Euclidean path integrals, Euclidean equations of motion, and the spectacular physics of **instantons** and tunneling
5. **The Big Connections** (Modules 12–13): The deep bridge to statistical mechanics and the extension to quantum field theory
6. **Frontiers** (Modules 14–15): Applications to lattice QCD, quantum gravity, condensed matter, and a complete cheat sheet

By the end, you will understand **why path integrals are the language of modern theoretical physics**.
:::

::: {.section-header}
### 📚 Prerequisites & Textbooks
:::

::: {.prereq-box}
#### 🧩 What You Should Know Before Starting
- **Quantum Mechanics**: The Schrödinger equation, Dirac notation $|x\rangle$, $\langle x | p \rangle$, time evolution operator $\hat{U} = e^{-i\hat{H}t/\hbar}$
- **Classical Mechanics**: Lagrangian $L = T - V$, the action $S = \int L\, dt$, Euler-Lagrange equations, Hamilton's principle
- **Mathematics**: Multivariable calculus, Gaussian integrals, Taylor series, linear algebra (eigenvalues), basic complex analysis
- **Helpful but not required**: [Quantum Harmonic Oscillator course](../QHO/index.qmd) on this site, statistical mechanics basics
:::

::: {.books-row}
<div class="book-pill">📖 Feynman & Hibbs<span>Quantum Mechanics and Path Integrals (original source)</span></div>
<div class="book-pill">📖 Shankar<span>Principles of QM, Chapters 8 & 21</span></div>
<div class="book-pill">📖 Zinn-Justin<span>QFT and Critical Phenomena</span></div>
<div class="book-pill">📖 Kleinert<span>Path Integrals in QM, Statistics & Polymer Physics</span></div>
<div class="book-pill">📖 Altland & Simons<span>Condensed Matter Field Theory</span></div>
<div class="book-pill">📖 Coleman<span>Aspects of Symmetry, Ch. 7 (Instantons)</span></div>
<div class="book-pill">📖 Peskin & Schroeder<span>An Introduction to QFT</span></div>
:::
